key_insight: Every simple connected GHZ graph with at least four vertices has dimension at most 2^(κ(G)−1) + κ(G)(κ(G)−1)/2, where κ(G) is vertex connectivity.
engineering_relevance: The bound links graph connectivity to achievable GHZ-state dimension, providing a theoretical constraint for graph-based photonic entanglement designs.
method: Use the graph representation of photonic experiments, where feasible monochromatic inherited vertex colourings determine GHZ dimension.
Prove an upper bound depending only on vertex connectivity.
Derive additional bounds involving edge connectivity and maximum degree.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports mathematical proofs, not experimental measurements or numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: The result applies to simple connected GHZ graphs and does not resolve the general conjecture that dimension is at most 2 for graphs with more than four vertices.
